capabilities.capability: Ready-to-run packages for Windows, macOS and Linux (an AppImage on Linux), so a workstation is set up in minutes.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios image every artist seat with the same build so files open identically everywhere.

match.note: Doodleberry runs in one Linux container; engine.doctor lists what is missing (Synfig among the tools) with the exact fix and tools/setup.sh applies it.

capabilities.capability: Stable and development builds that can be installed side by side, so new features can be tried without risking production files.
capabilities.pro_use: Leads trial a development build on a copy of a shot before the team upgrades.

match.note: One pinned toolchain per container; engine.info reports the versions found. A second environment is a second container, not a second install.

capabilities.capability: Building the application from source (Autotools, CMake from 1.5, vcpkg), with reproducible builds from 1.5.3.
capabilities.pro_use: Pipeline teams patch the renderer and ship an in-house build.

match.note: vendor.build runs a vendored component's upstream build recipe in a copy; vendor.check verifies its upstream record and licence. Synfig core itself is not vendored yet (WP-34 decides drive vs vendor).

capabilities.capability: A first animation from scratch: draw a few shapes, key them at two times, render a movie.
capabilities.pro_use: Onboarding and quick tests of an idea before a real shot is set up.

match.note: A film folder from scratch or a format template, rendered with QA in one command; the doodle flow (doodle.snap) gets a talking character in seconds.

capabilities.capability: A basic cut-out rig with bones on separate drawn parts.
capabilities.pro_use: The standard way to make a reusable character for a series.

match.note: Layered drawings become rigged puppets by layer name; cast.generate makes an original rigged humanoid.

capabilities.capability: Basic masking: show one piece of artwork only inside another shape.
capabilities.pro_use: Mouths inside heads, reveals, wipes and eye-in-socket tricks.

match.note: No general mask in puppet or shot data (only internal clipping in toon shading and mesh triangles); masks and mattes belong to the compositor WP.

capabilities.capability: Dockable panels with workspace layouts that can be saved and switched (1.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Artists keep separate layouts for drawing, rigging and timing.

match.note: Agent-native: the command registry (engine.commands) is the interface; Studio pages are fixed views over the same commands.

capabilities.capability: Layers panel: the stacked tree of layers and groups, with show/hide, reordering, grouping and renaming.
capabilities.pro_use: Organising a character into named parts and keeping heavy scenes navigable.

match.note: The part tree and its z order live in the puppet; shot layers (set, underlays, cast, overlays) in shots.json. No layer-tree editor in Studio; the Rig Canvas edits parts.

capabilities.capability: Parameters panel: every parameter of the selected layer is editable numerically, including sub-parameters of converted values.
capabilities.pro_use: Precise values for placement, colours and timing that are hard to drag by hand.

match.note: Every field of a film is plain JSON, read with film.get and written (schema-validated) with film.write.

capabilities.capability: Timetrack panel: waypoints of every parameter aligned to the time bar, with box selection, dragging, duplicating and scaling (rewritten in 1.5.0).
capabilities.pro_use: Retiming a performance by shifting or compressing groups of keys.

match.note: The Studio timeline moves, resizes, adds and deletes clip layers (line-relative); per-key lanes, camera-key lane and line/shot dragging are WP-19.

capabilities.capability: History panel: an undo/redo list where individual past actions can be toggled off.
capabilities.pro_use: Safe experimentation and backing out of a change made several steps ago.

match.note: Films are text under git (any version re-renders exactly) and the Studio timeline keeps an undo stack; a per-change audit log of who changed what is WP-39.

capabilities.capability: Info panel: pointer coordinates and colour, and render progress (progress bar from 1.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Checking exact positions and watching long renders.

match.note: Jobs run async and report progress events, posted to webhooks when given (WP-20).

capabilities.capability: Palette editor: a document palette of named colours, loadable and savable, applied to selected shapes.
capabilities.pro_use: Keeping a character's colour model consistent across every shot.

match.note: Strokes reference named palette slots, so recolouring is a data change; puppet.lint flags raw colours and brand.check measures the brand palette.

capabilities.capability: Sets panel: named selections of layers scattered through the document, selected or switched off together.
capabilities.pro_use: Toggling all of a prop's pieces, or selecting all left-side parts at once.

match.note: No named part selections in the Rig Canvas or data (clip tracks target parts one by one); should join WP-18 (Rig Canvas 2).

capabilities.capability: Navigator and canvas browser: a thumbnail for panning a zoomed view, and a browser of open files and their nested canvases.
capabilities.pro_use: Moving around large backgrounds and multi-canvas files.

match.note: View navigation is a desktop UI concern; films and their files are listed by film.get.

capabilities.capability: Canvas properties: pixel size, image area in units, frame rate, start and end time, background.
capabilities.pro_use: Setting a delivery format once per project.

match.note: Size and fps are film fields; qa.run enforces 1080x1920 at 30 fps; shot times may be line-relative.

capabilities.capability: Resizing the canvas with presets and a keep-aspect option (1.5.1, 1.5.3).
capabilities.pro_use: Making a square or landscape version of a vertical piece.

match.note: film.render with aspect 16:9 or 1:1 re-stages the film for the new frame rather than cropping; one command for all aspects is WP-24.

capabilities.capability: Per-document gamma (1.4; new files linear at 1.0, old files kept at 2.2).
capabilities.pro_use: Matching colour blending to the rest of the pipeline.

match.note: Colours are plain sRGB in the browser and ffmpeg; managed colour (OCIO, ACES) is WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Grid with snapping for placing handles.
capabilities.pro_use: Aligning layout elements and mechanical props.

match.note: Positions are numbers in data written by agents or commands; there is no hand placement to snap.

capabilities.capability: Rulers and guides, rotatable and editable from 1.5.3.
capabilities.pro_use: Marking title-safe areas, horizons and eye lines.

match.note: Instead of drawn guides, qa.run measures every word's box against the platform-safe area and type minimums; brand.assets writes safe-area overlays.

capabilities.capability: Workarea preview quality modes, background rendering and a frame cache for smooth scrubbing (1.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Judging motion interactively in heavy scenes.

match.note: The player page renders every frame as a pure function of time, so it scrubs live in the browser.

capabilities.capability: Preview render of a time range at reduced size and frame rate.
capabilities.pro_use: Quick timing checks before a full render.

match.note: Animatic over the sound in seconds, live preview, and a storyboard strip.

capabilities.capability: Onion skin: faint past and future frames, counted in frames or in keyframes (1.4, 1.5.1).
capabilities.pro_use: Spacing and arcs while keying poses.

match.note: The Rig Canvas onion shows only the rest pose; onion skins over time come with hand-drawn animation (WP-35), boards with onion skin in WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Animate editing mode: edits either change the base value or create waypoints at the current time.
capabilities.pro_use: Separating rig setup from animation without accidental keys.

match.note: Separation is structural: the puppet holds the rest state, the shot timeline holds everything that changes.

capabilities.capability: On-canvas handles and the group transformation widget (move, rotate, scale, move the origin) for direct manipulation.
capabilities.pro_use: Posing and placing by hand rather than by numbers.

match.note: The Rig Canvas poses by dragging hands and feet (IK) and puppet.save keeps poses and clips; dragging characters, camera and lines within a shot is WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Canvas dependencies dialog listing external files with path relinking (1.5.3).
capabilities.pro_use: Collecting and repairing a project's assets before hand-off.

match.note: Every file that shapes a film is listed with its licence class; paths are data, so relinking is a film.write.

capabilities.capability: Colours dialog (RGB, HSV, hex, alpha) and defaults for new layers (fill and outline colours, width, blend).
capabilities.pro_use: House colours and line weights applied to every new shape.

match.note: Palette slots and brand kit defaults; brand.check measures contrast and colour-blind separation.

capabilities.capability: Transform, smooth move, scale and rotate tools for selecting and manipulating layers and vertices, with box selection.
capabilities.pro_use: Day-to-day posing and layout.

match.note: Posing by drag in the Rig Canvas and clip edits in the timeline; in-shot transforms of characters and props are data only until WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Spline tool: a Bezier pen that makes a region, outline, advanced outline, plant or curve gradient from one path in one pass.
capabilities.pro_use: Clean vector character lines with editable tangents.

match.note: Strokes are SVG paths; the Rig Canvas draws freehand ink and drawing.fulfil lifts ink into parts, but there is no Bezier pen with tangent handles or polygon editing (WP-18).

capabilities.capability: Draw tool: freehand strokes fitted to splines with smoothing, optional pressure-driven width.
capabilities.pro_use: Sketch-quality lines that stay editable vectors.

match.note: Rig Canvas pressure ink with simplify (perfect-freehand); stabiliser, textured brushes, lasso and transform remain in WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Sketch tool: rough guide strokes that are never rendered, saved and reloaded separately (redo from 1.5.5).
capabilities.pro_use: Roughing poses and layout before clean-up.

match.note: Drawing requests carry ghost guides and puppet.import skips sketch and guide layers; a sketch layer inside the Rig Canvas is not there (WP-18).

capabilities.capability: Width tool: brush along an outline to thicken or thin it locally.
capabilities.pro_use: Line weight that tapers into joints and swells on curves.

match.note: Strokes carry one width; editing width along a line belongs with Rig Canvas tools 2.

capabilities.capability: Fill and eyedrop tools: fill a closed area with the current colour, pick a colour from the canvas (fill colour on Ctrl+click from 1.5).
capabilities.pro_use: Fast colouring of line art.

match.note: The Rig Canvas gap-closing fill writes a palette slot name into the stroke; picking is by slot name, not by sampling.

capabilities.capability: Circle, rectangle, star and polygon tools creating parametric shapes as chosen layer types.
capabilities.pro_use: Props, graphic elements and motion-design shapes.

match.note: Any static primitive is an SVG path; animatable parametric primitives (radius, point count) do not exist and would join WP-42 (procedural 2D).

capabilities.capability: Gradient tool: drag to create linear, radial, conical or spiral gradient layers.
capabilities.pro_use: Sky ramps, soft shading and lighting passes.

match.note: Gradients are flattened on import and absent from puppet and shot data; should join WP-36 (compositor) as generator nodes.

capabilities.capability: Text tool: place a text layer, then edit text, font, size and orientation.
capabilities.pro_use: Titles, labels and signage.

ref: shots.json overlays (text, title, sign, paper, card)
match.note: Timed text elements with fonts from the brand kit; type sizes measured by qa.run.

capabilities.capability: Mirror tool: reflect selected vertices across a horizontal or vertical axis.
capabilities.pro_use: Building symmetric drawings and flipping poses.

match.note: No mirror operation on strokes or poses (puppet.coach only reports left/right mismatch); should join WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Cutout tool: draw a polygon to cut a region out of an image layer.
capabilities.pro_use: Splitting a painted character into animatable parts.

match.note: Parts are cut from one ink layer by polygons with overlap seams that hide the cut.

capabilities.capability: Brush tool (experimental, MyPaint-based) for raster painting on image layers.
capabilities.pro_use: Painted texture, backgrounds and touch-ups inside the animation file.

match.note: No raster painting; WP-34 picks the brush engine (libmypaint, Krita) and WP-35/WP-18 build on it.

capabilities.capability: Region layer: a filled area bounded by a spline whose vertices can be animated.
capabilities.pro_use: Fills of character parts and backgrounds.

match.note: Filled paths per part; the path itself is static per drawing (shape changes are swaps, bends or mesh skinning).

capabilities.capability: Outline layer: a stroke along a spline with per-vertex width, round tips and sharp or smooth cusps.
capabilities.pro_use: Ink lines of characters.

match.note: Strokes have one width and round caps; export.synfig writes them as outline layers.

capabilities.capability: Advanced outline: width points independent of vertices, dashes, several tip styles (two new dash tips in 1.4), smoothing.
capabilities.pro_use: Expressive tapered ink and dashed lines.

match.note: No variable-width or dashed character lines (only dashed whisper bubbles); line media simulation is WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Animating spline vertices directly: shapes morph between keyed outlines.
capabilities.pro_use: Shape tweens for cloth, mouths and squash without swaps.

match.note: Shapes deform by bendy limbs and skinned mesh strokes (SVG only); there is no per-vertex keyed morph, and morphs between drawings are WP-43.

capabilities.capability: Parametric circle, rectangle (rounded corners, feather; 1.4), star and polygon layers with animatable parameters.
capabilities.pro_use: Motion graphics shapes whose radius or point count animates.

match.note: Static paths and kit elements only; animated parametric primitives should join WP-42 (procedural 2D).

capabilities.capability: Solid colour layer filling the canvas or group.
capabilities.pro_use: Backgrounds and colour holds.

match.note: The plain set with a colour option; exporters write a background colour or the set plate.

capabilities.capability: Feathered (soft) shape edges.
capabilities.pro_use: Soft shadows, glows and light pools.

match.note: No soft-edge shapes in data; blurs and mattes come with the compositor.

capabilities.capability: Winding style (non-zero or even-odd) to make holes in self-overlapping regions.
capabilities.pro_use: Rings, letters and cut-through shapes from one path.

match.note: Strokes take a fill rule (rule: evenodd) that cuts holes; Lottie and Synfig write it, Grease Pencil gets keyhole polygons.

capabilities.capability: Linear and radial gradient layers with animatable endpoints and colour stops.
capabilities.pro_use: Skies, vignettes, soft lighting and depth fades.

match.note: Only sets drawn in code use gradients; nothing in puppet or shot data. Should join WP-36 (compositor generator nodes). The AI-look lint (WP-04) also limits large gradient fills.

capabilities.capability: Conical and spiral gradient layers.
capabilities.pro_use: Radar sweeps, stylised backgrounds, hypnotic effects.

match.note: Same as linear/radial: join WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Curve gradient: a gradient laid along a spline with a width, for shading along edges.
capabilities.pro_use: Rim shading and form shading that follows a contour.

match.note: style.toon gives cel shadow bands and rim light from a fixed light in the SVG renderer; other renderers (Synfig, Lottie, Grease Pencil) are WP-14.

capabilities.capability: Noise gradient: animated procedural noise mapped to a gradient.
capabilities.pro_use: Textures, clouds, flicker and film grain.

match.note: Seeded grain and turbulent line boil, both deterministic; not a general noise fill.

capabilities.capability: Gradient editor dialog and gradient converters (rotate, repeat, two-tone, gradient colour) to edit and reuse gradients.
capabilities.pro_use: House gradients shared across shots.

match.note: No gradient data type; join WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Colour correct layer: hue shift, brightness, contrast, exposure, gamma and (1.5.5) saturation on everything below it.
capabilities.pro_use: Shot grading and matching a character to a background.

match.note: shots.json post (grade, LUT, vignette, presets) grades the joined picture; per-layer correction inside a shot is WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Clamp layer: keep colour values within a range (no negatives, a ceiling on brightness).
capabilities.pro_use: Cleaning up results of additive blends before output.

match.note: The 8-bit sRGB path cannot go out of range; a float or HDR pipeline (WP-37) would need clamping.

capabilities.capability: Luma key: turn brightness into transparency.
capabilities.pro_use: Using scanned line art or light effects over other layers.

match.note: Ink import thresholds a scan's ink to alpha at import time; a keying node inside a shot is WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Chroma key layer with invert (1.5.3).
capabilities.pro_use: Compositing green-screen footage or flat-colour plates.

match.note: No footage keying; compositor WP.

capabilities.capability: Halftone 2 and halftone 3 layers: print-style dot screens.
capabilities.pro_use: Comic and retro print looks.

match.note: Style passes cover paper, grain and boil; a halftone pass fits WP-15's medium simulation.

capabilities.capability: Filters act on everything below them in their group, so effects can be scoped by grouping.
capabilities.pro_use: Grading only the background, or only one character.

match.note: Effects are whole-frame (post) or built in; scoped effect stacks need the per-shot node compositor.

capabilities.capability: Blur layer with several kernels (box, fast Gaussian, cross, Gaussian, disc) on the content below.
capabilities.pro_use: Soft shadows, glows and out-of-focus backgrounds.

match.note: No blur in shot or puppet data.

capabilities.capability: Motion blur layer: accumulates sub-frame samples over an aperture; can leave a sharp trail instead (1.5.3).
capabilities.pro_use: Fast action that reads smoothly; ghosted trails as a stylistic effect.

match.note: Speed lines are drawn from motion (fx), but sub-frame motion blur is open in WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Radial blur: a zoom-burst blur from a centre point.
capabilities.pro_use: Impact frames and dramatic push-ins.

match.note: Impact stars exist (fx.impacts) but no radial blur.

capabilities.capability: Depth-of-field effects by blurring far layers.
capabilities.pro_use: Focusing the eye on the speaking character.

match.note: Multiplane depth of field is in WP-36's scope.

capabilities.capability: Curve warp: bends the artwork below along a spline.
capabilities.pro_use: Rubber-hose limbs, tails and bending props without redrawing.

match.note: puppet bend curves a part along the joint's arc and chains bend tails (SVG and Grease Pencil); not along an arbitrary spline, and Synfig/Lottie output stays rigid until WP-14.

capabilities.capability: Noise distort: turbulent displacement of the content below, animatable.
capabilities.pro_use: Wobbly hand-drawn lines, heat haze, water.

match.note: Deterministic cycled displacement fields make line boil on characters, bubbles and props.

capabilities.capability: Spherize, twirl, stretch and inside-out lens distortions.
capabilities.pro_use: Cartoon bulges, dizzy spins, comedic stretches.

match.note: No distortion nodes; compositor WP.

capabilities.capability: Perspective layer (the rewritten warp layer, 1.5.0): four-corner perspective warp of everything below, with interpolation quality.
capabilities.pro_use: Putting a flat drawing on a wall, a floor or a screen in the scene.

match.note: 2D layers in 3D exist only in the three.js renderer; layers on planes with a camera are WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Translate, rotate and scale layers that transform everything below them in their group.
capabilities.pro_use: Moving a whole character or scene section at once.

match.note: Characters are placed by keyed position and scale; parts rotate about pivots down the hierarchy.

capabilities.capability: Group transformation with offset, angle, skew, scale and a movable origin (1.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Rigging nested pieces and adding a lean or shear.

match.note: Rotation about pivots, shifts and whole-body squash; skew and per-part squash are missing (per-part squash and stretch is WP-11).

capabilities.capability: Camera moves made by transforming a top-level group (pan, zoom, rotate).
capabilities.pro_use: Pans, push-ins and shakes in a scene without a camera object.

match.note: Camera keys and automatic coverage (speaker framing, punch-ins, handheld) are baked for every renderer; camera roll is not supported.

capabilities.capability: Shade layer: a drop shadow (or inner shadow, inverted) made from the alpha below, with offset, softness and colour.
capabilities.pro_use: Lifting characters off the background, and graphic-style shadows.

match.note: Ground shadows under characters and cel shadows (style.toon) exist; a general drop or inner shadow from alpha needs the compositor.

capabilities.capability: Bevel layer: a light and dark edge that makes shapes look embossed (handles on parameters from 1.5.3).
capabilities.pro_use: Buttons, logos and a soft 3D finish on props.

match.note: style.toon's rim light and shadow band give a similar edge on filled vector shapes in SVG; other renderers are WP-14.

capabilities.capability: Animating the light angle, depth and softness of shade and bevel over time.
capabilities.pro_use: Lighting that changes as a lamp swings or the sun sets.

match.note: The toon light is fixed per shot; animated lighting with the compositor (time-of-day grades also touch WP-37).

capabilities.capability: Time loop layer: repeats a span of the animation below (local start, duration, link time).
capabilities.pro_use: Walk cycles, blinking lights, idling crowds.

match.note: Library and character clips loop (idle, walk); chains carry a travelling wave.

capabilities.capability: Stroboscope layer: samples the animation below at a lower rate.
capabilities.pro_use: Animating on twos or threes for a hand-made feel.

match.note: Stepped timing on 12s, 8s or 6s per shot or character; repeated frames are deduplicated at render.

capabilities.capability: Time offset and speed on groups and imported canvases: shift, slow, speed up or freeze a nested animation.
capabilities.pro_use: Reusing one animation at a different moment or tempo.

match.note: Clips are placed on the words and play at a tempo; timewarp holds and slows a shot (SVG player only).

chapters.chapter: Layers: other (group, switch, duplicate, image, text, procedural)

capabilities.capability: Group layer: nests layers into a sub-canvas with its own transform, time offset, z range and outline grow.
capabilities.pro_use: Building a character as nested parts and reusing groups.

match.note: Parts form the hierarchy; export.synfig writes one group per part.

capabilities.capability: Switch group: shows exactly one child, chosen by name or (1.4) by depth index, animatable.
capabilities.pro_use: Mouth charts, hand poses, eye sets and outfit changes.

match.note: Swap sets and views, driven by visemes, clips and controls; exported to Synfig as hold-keyed visibility.

capabilities.capability: Duplicate layer: repeats its group with an index value, so copies can vary by index.
capabilities.pro_use: Radial patterns, rows of objects, simple crowds.

match.note: Seeded scatter and instancing of cast members and 3D blocks with per-copy variation; duplicating a group by index is WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Import image layer: a bitmap placed by its corners, openable in an external editor and reloaded (1.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Painted backgrounds and raster character parts.

match.note: Raster-part puppets from scans or PSD/ORA, and a layered file out to an artist and back (raster parts render in SVG only, WP-14).

capabilities.capability: Text layer: font family list, size, orientation, spacing, animatable text; rewritten in 1.5.1 with right-to-left support and a direction parameter.
capabilities.pro_use: Titles, captions and signage in several languages.

match.note: Text overlays, bubbles and captions with Sinhala fallback; right-to-left and complex scripts are WP-25.

capabilities.capability: Plant layer: procedural branching growth along a spline.
capabilities.pro_use: Growing vines, roots and hair-like flourishes.

match.note: The kit's roots element grows a root system timed to lines; general procedural growth is WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Super sample layer: renders a group at higher resolution for cleaner antialiasing.
capabilities.pro_use: Fixing jaggies on fine detail.

match.note: Vector parts are rasterised by Chromium at output resolution with antialiasing; nothing to supersample.

capabilities.capability: Procedural generator layers: checkerboard, XOR pattern, metaballs, Mandelbrot and Julia fractals.
capabilities.pro_use: Backgrounds, test patterns and abstract motion design.

match.note: Procedural 2D layer scope.

capabilities.capability: Blend methods per layer: composite, straight, onto, behind, screen, overlay, hard light, multiply, divide, add, subtract, difference, brighten, darken, colour, hue, saturation, luminance, alpha over, and alpha intersection (1.5.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Shading, lighting passes, glows and graphic colour effects.

match.note: Everything composites normally; blend modes are in the compositor scope.

capabilities.capability: Masking through blends: draw a layer only onto what is below, or use one layer's alpha to cut another.
capabilities.pro_use: Clothing patterns inside a shape, shading clipped to a body part.

match.note: Only internal self-clipping (toon shading) exists.

capabilities.capability: Opacity (amount) per layer, animatable.
capabilities.pro_use: Fades, ghosts and dissolving effects.

match.note: Strokes have a static opacity and swaps/views switch by visibility; animated opacity on parts and layers is not in data (would sit with WP-36; dissolves between shots are WP-15).

capabilities.capability: Z-depth parameter: moves a layer within its group's order, animatable.
capabilities.pro_use: An arm passing in front of then behind the body.

match.note: pose.z, clip swaps.z and controls drive order in SVG and Grease Pencil; Synfig and Lottie exports keep a static order (WP-14).

capabilities.capability: Origin and focus point parameters: the pivot for transforms and the centre for effects.
capabilities.pro_use: Rotating parts about joints.

match.note: Pivots per part, estimated on import and checked by puppet.coach.

capabilities.capability: Invert parameter: a shape becomes a hole that shows everything outside it.
capabilities.pro_use: Iris wipes, spotlights and cut-through windows.

match.note: No inverted shapes or mattes; an iris between shots is a transition (WP-15).

capabilities.capability: Antialias switch and feather per shape.
capabilities.pro_use: Crisp pixel-art edges, or softened edges.

match.note: Antialiasing is always on in the browser rasteriser; soft edges are covered under geometry feathering (WP-36).

capabilities.capability: Skeleton layer: a hierarchy of bones (origin, angle, length, width, tip width, depth) that is shown while editing and never rendered.
capabilities.pro_use: Cut-out character rigs.

match.note: Each part is a bone with a pivot and joint limits; FK, two-bone IK and FABRIK chains are in the loader.

capabilities.capability: Skeleton tool (1.5.0): click to create bones and re-parent them.
capabilities.pro_use: Rigging new characters quickly.

match.note: Rigs come from templates (humanoid, doodle) with pivots from markers or estimated; free-form hierarchies such as quadrupeds and birds are WP-16 templates.

capabilities.capability: Link to bone: attach chosen vertices to one bone so they move rigidly with it.
capabilities.pro_use: Rigid cut-out pieces such as a forearm or a shoe.

match.note: Strokes belong to a part and follow it rigidly.

capabilities.capability: Link to skeleton: vertices are bound to every bone whose influence shape covers them, weighted by coverage; weights are editable.
capabilities.pro_use: Smooth bends at elbows, knees and torsos from one drawing.

match.note: Skinned mesh strokes carry per-vertex part weights (from Blender rigs) and bend in SVG; automatic weighting of vector strokes is missing and should join WP-11.

capabilities.capability: Skeleton deformation layer: bones warp raster artwork below through a subdivided mesh, with a rest pose reset.
capabilities.pro_use: Bending painted characters without cutting them into pieces.

match.note: Mesh strokes give this in the SVG renderer; the .sif exporter does not write Skeleton Deformation, which the feature map assigns to WP-14.

capabilities.capability: Bone link and bone influence converters: any parameter (a prop's position, a value) follows a bone.
capabilities.pro_use: Props held in hands, accessories that follow the head.

match.note: Props attach to parts and move hand to hand; look-at aims a part at another character's part (SVG player).

capabilities.capability: Changing a bone's parent during the animation.
capabilities.pro_use: Passing an object between hands, or a character picking something up.

match.note: Parent switching for props with travel arcs; parts of a character keep a fixed hierarchy.

capabilities.capability: Bone length scaling (local and recursive) to stretch limbs.
capabilities.pro_use: Cartoon stretch on reaches and jumps.

match.note: Per-part scale along the bone (local, carrying the children's pivots) and stretchy IK limbs; a recursive scale that also scales the children is WP-11.

capabilities.capability: Rest pose versus animated pose (reset pose), and a quick humanoid skeleton from a bundled plugin (add-skeleton-simple; image-as-stickman).
capabilities.pro_use: Starting rigs from a standard template.

match.note: Every puppet has a rest pose and named poses; cast.generate builds a rigged original from a short spec; puppet.sheet shows rest and key poses.

capabilities.capability: Arithmetic converters: add, subtract, scale, reciprocal, power, exponential, logarithm, modulo, absolute (1.5.5), range and map range (1.5.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Driving one value from another with a formula, such as a wheel turning with distance.

match.note: puppet.json controls drive targets through piecewise-linear key curves (covers map range and scale), and every renderer plays them; general expressions on any field would join WP-42's rules.

capabilities.capability: Trigonometric and vector converters: sine, cosine, atan2, dot product, vector angle, length, X and Y, composite and radial composite.
capabilities.pro_use: Oscillations, orbits and values split into components for separate animation.

match.note: Built-in oscillators exist (chain wave, idle noise, camera float), but no general trig driver on arbitrary fields (WP-42).

capabilities.capability: Logic and comparison converters: and, or, not, compare, switch between values by a condition.
capabilities.pro_use: Rig switches: show the hand pose that matches a control.

match.note: controls can drive discrete swaps (swap.<id>) by value, which covers switch-by-threshold; boolean logic is absent.

capabilities.capability: Linear converter: a value that changes at a constant rate over time.
capabilities.pro_use: Spinning wheels, drifting clouds, ticking clocks.

match.note: Props spin, sets drift and the camera floats; not available on every field.

capabilities.capability: Random converter: seeded smooth random motion with speed, radius and loop.
capabilities.pro_use: Jitter, handheld camera and flicker that stay repeatable.

match.note: Seeded noise everywhere; frames are pure functions of the frame number.

capabilities.capability: Spline converters (spline, vertex, tangent, width, segment): bind a value to a point or tangent along a path.
capabilities.pro_use: Objects travelling along paths and orienting to them.

match.note: Positions of characters and props are bound to splines by arc length; binding other values to spline points or tangents is WP-20.

capabilities.capability: Dynamic converter: a point with mass, spring and damping that lags and overshoots its target.
capabilities.pro_use: Follow-through on hair, ears, antennae and props.

match.note: Deterministic spring re-simulation on parts; prop physics solved at bake time.

capabilities.capability: Animation from file converter: values read from an external file (Papagayo and Rhubarb lip-sync; more value types in 1.5).
capabilities.pro_use: Driving a mouth switch from a lip-sync tool's output.

match.note: Visemes come from the voice alignment (voice.build); data-bound overlays read analysis output (film.data). Arbitrary fields cannot be fed from a file.

capabilities.capability: String converters (integer, real, angle and time to text).
capabilities.pro_use: On-screen counters, timers and debug readouts.

match.note: Animated counters with prefix, suffix and decimals; values can come from data.json.

capabilities.capability: Time-shaping converters: step, timed swap, time loop and reverse, applied to a single parameter.
capabilities.pro_use: Stepping one element on twos while the rest moves smoothly; reversing a move.

match.note: style.step works per shot or character and timewarp per shot; per-parameter stepping and reversed clips are not there (12-fps-native stepped rendering is WP-15).

capabilities.capability: Colour converters: greyed, gradient colour, two-tone, stripes.
capabilities.pro_use: Desaturated flashbacks, colour cycling and patterned fills.

match.note: Runtime recolour exists through palette slots; palette variants per scene (night, sick, cold) are WP-16.

capabilities.capability: Average, weighted average and derivative converters.
capabilities.pro_use: Blending between poses, and reacting to speed.

match.note: Clips blend by weight with fades; speed lines and dust are computed from motion speed.

chapters.chapter: Linking, exported values and the library

capabilities.capability: Linking: several parameters share one value, so moving one handle moves all linked ones.
capabilities.pro_use: Joints that never gap and colours that change together.

match.note: Colours link through slots; joints share pivots with overlap so bends do not gap (checked by puppet.coach).

capabilities.capability: Exporting a value to the library under a name, then connecting it elsewhere; exported values keep their animation.
capabilities.pro_use: A shared light angle or colour scheme across a whole shot.

match.note: Named poses, brand values and clips are reusable by name; there is no named value shared between arbitrary shot fields.

capabilities.capability: Exported canvases: nested animations stored once (also in other files) and reused as many instances.
capabilities.pro_use: A walk cycle or a prop animation reused across shots and files.

match.note: Characters and their own clips live in the cast library with provenance and content hashes; shots reference them by path.

capabilities.capability: Reusing an animation on a different character by importing a file with exported values.
capabilities.pro_use: One library of motion for a whole cast.

match.note: Clips are template-level, so every character on a template plays them (retargeting across characters).

capabilities.capability: Static parameters: mark a value so it cannot be animated by accident.
capabilities.pro_use: Locking rig settings while animating.

match.note: Rig values live in the puppet and only timeline fields animate; nothing in the rig can be keyed by accident.

chapters.chapter: Animation: waypoints, interpolation, keyframes and the time track

capabilities.capability: Any parameter change in animation mode creates a waypoint at the current time.
capabilities.pro_use: Pose-to-pose keying directly on the canvas.

match.note: Keys are written as data (place, look, ik, controls, camera) and clips are added in the timeline; the Rig Canvas records keyed poses into clips. Per-key editing in Studio is WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Waypoint editing: select, drag, duplicate and scale groups of waypoints; jump between them (1.5.0).
capabilities.pro_use: Retiming and polishing a performance.

match.note: Clip layers move and resize; individual keys inside a clip and key scaling are WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Interpolation per waypoint side: clamped, TCB (tension, continuity, bias), constant, ease in/out and linear; changed in bulk from 1.5.3.
capabilities.pro_use: Holds, snaps, smooth arcs and overshoot shaped key by key.

match.note: Clip keys always ease with smoothstep, swaps and views hold, anticipation/overshoot comes from acting.principles; choosing interpolation per key needs the curve editor of WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Keyframes: named marks across all parameters; changing a keyframe's length shifts every later waypoint.
capabilities.pro_use: Retiming a whole scene section without touching individual keys.

match.note: Spoken lines play the role of keyframes: times are line-relative, so re-voicing or retiming moves everything after it.

capabilities.capability: Keyframe locks for past and future keyframes (hotkeys in 1.5.4), so editing between keys keeps neighbouring poses.
capabilities.pro_use: Protecting finished poses while adjusting an in-between.

match.note: Clips are separate layers with their own start and end; editing one never writes keys into neighbours.

capabilities.capability: Keyframe activation toggle and description notes.
capabilities.pro_use: Labelling story beats on the time bar.

match.note: Lines are named beats; review notes pin comments to frames (review.add).

capabilities.capability: Time track with playback range, looped playback, frame previews on hover and markers for segments with constant value (1.4, 1.5).
capabilities.pro_use: Reviewing a section repeatedly while timing it.

match.note: The Studio timeline scrubs with live preview over clip and dialogue lanes; per-parameter lanes, camera lane and graph view are WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Graphs panel: value curves with draggable control points and tangents, multi-select, nudging (1.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Fine-tuning ease and spacing.

match.note: Curve (graph) editor is in WP-19's scope.

capabilities.capability: Baking: turn an interpolated or converted parameter into one waypoint per frame (1.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Freezing procedural motion for export or hand-editing.

match.note: All renderers read the baked animation (tools/bake.mjs); the exporters write per-frame keys from it.

capabilities.capability: Copying and pasting waypoints or whole poses to other times.
capabilities.pro_use: Reusing a key pose later in the shot.

match.note: Named poses can be placed at any time; clips can be added again with timeline.edit.

capabilities.capability: Sound layer: an audio file placed with a delay and volume (audio is not rendered into the output file).
capabilities.pro_use: Animating to dialogue and music in the scene.

match.note: Voices are synthesised and aligned, and film.render mixes voice, score, cues and foley and muxes them with the picture.

capabilities.capability: Sound panel with a waveform for syncing (1.4), with a choice of which sound layer to show (1.5.0).
capabilities.pro_use: Hitting accents and phonemes by eye.

match.note: Waveform lanes of each stem on the Studio sound page, with words and beats known from timing.json.

capabilities.capability: Audio playback while scrubbing and playing in the workarea.
capabilities.pro_use: Checking sync interactively.

match.note: The web player and animatic play with sound; editing and scrubbing audio cues in the timeline is WP-40.

capabilities.capability: Lip-sync import from Papagayo (.pgo) and Rhubarb (TSV/XML, 1.5.0) driving a switch group of mouths.
capabilities.pro_use: Fast dialogue animation from a breakdown.

match.note: Visemes come from phoneme timings automatically; lipsync.check measures sync against the voice and against Rhubarb when installed.

capabilities.capability: Per-layer volume.
capabilities.pro_use: Balancing dialogue, music and effects.

match.note: The mix is rule-based (ducking, effects under music) and measured: -14 LUFS, true peak, effect onsets; mixcheck checks intelligibility.

capabilities.capability: Joining sound and picture after rendering with an external tool (the manual suggests ffmpeg).
capabilities.pro_use: Delivering a finished movie with audio.

match.note: Muxing is part of the render, with captions (.srt, .vtt) and QA.

capabilities.capability: Bitmap import (PNG, JPEG and more; many formats through Magick++ from 1.5.3) with scale-to-fit (1.5.0).
capabilities.pro_use: Bringing in painted backgrounds and character art.

match.note: Scans and photos become raster-part puppets; layered PSD/ORA become puppets by layer name.

capabilities.capability: Image sequence import as an animated layer, skipping duplicate frames (1.4, 1.5.0).
capabilities.pro_use: Bringing hand-drawn frame-by-frame animation or renders into a scene.

match.note: Drawn levels (a sequence of drawings with exposures) are WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Vectorization: bitmaps traced into outline layers (centreline and outline modes, ported from OpenToonz, 1.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Turning paper drawings into editable vectors.

match.note: Ink import keeps raster lines; vector tracing (VTracer, potrace) is WP-18.

capabilities.capability: SVG import into layers (groups, paths, colours; SVG text from 1.5.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Bringing in art made in Inkscape or Illustrator.

match.note: Layered SVG becomes a vector puppet; colours become palette slots and transforms and gradients are flattened.

capabilities.capability: Video import as a layer (basic; slow on large files).
capabilities.pro_use: Reference footage for rotoscoping and timing.

match.note: Video of a person becomes an action clip (pose and face retargeting); footage as a layer in a shot, for reference or compositing, belongs with WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Swf2svg: a helper to convert Flash files to SVG.
capabilities.pro_use: Migrating old Flash libraries.

match.note: No Flash legacy to migrate; SVG import covers converted files.

capabilities.capability: Round trip of an image layer through an external editor (1.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Painting fixes in a raster editor and seeing them in the scene.

match.note: A puppet goes out as a layered SVG, ORA or PSD and comes back by layer name.

capabilities.capability: Render dialog: target, file name, image size, quality, antialiasing, a time range or a single frame.
capabilities.pro_use: Final renders and test renders of a section.

match.note: One shot or the whole film; film.render only re-renders changed shots (content hash).

capabilities.capability: Output targets: PNG and PNG sequences, GIF, BMP, ffmpeg video (AVI default from 1.4, lossless H.264, WebM from 1.5.3), ImageMagick formats.
capabilities.pro_use: Delivering to editors, the web and print.

match.note: H.264 MP4 with per-platform encoding profiles; WebM and ProRes with alpha (shot.alpha), GIF and APNG (film.formats) and sticker packs (sticker.pack) (WP-23).

capabilities.capability: Headless command-line rendering: choose file, target, output, size, start and end time, frame rate.
capabilities.pro_use: Batch and farm rendering from scripts.

match.note: shot.render with renderer synfig writes the .sif and drives the Synfig CLI; characters render with alpha and are composited over the SVG set.

capabilities.capability: Multithreaded rendering with a thread count (preferences from 1.5.0) and render engine choice on the command line (1.5.3).
capabilities.pro_use: Using every core and choosing speed versus quality.

match.note: One browser worker per CPU with frame dedupe; renderer choice per shot. Distributed workers across machines are WP-38.

capabilities.capability: Rendering one exported canvas instead of the root, and listing canvases.
capabilities.pro_use: Rendering a single element or variant from a master file.

match.note: Single shots, and hook variants as alternative openings joined to the rest of the film.

capabilities.capability: Alpha output, including writing alpha to a separate file.
capabilities.pro_use: Handing characters to a compositor over separate backgrounds.

match.note: Synfig and Grease Pencil renders are made with alpha internally and composited; shot.alpha delivers WebM and ProRes with alpha (WP-23); EXR passes are WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Render progress output, stopping a render (1.5.0) and a notification when done.
capabilities.pro_use: Managing long renders.

match.note: Renders run as async jobs with progress events and webhooks (WP-20); owner notifications are WP-03.

capabilities.capability: Benchmarks and repeated renders of the same target (-b, --set-repeats in 1.5.3).
capabilities.pro_use: Measuring render cost before committing a farm.

match.note: render.estimate gives the time before rendering from measured rates and per-shot probes (WP-20).

capabilities.capability: Physical resolution (DPI) for print output.
capabilities.pro_use: Posters, books and merchandise stills.

match.note: film.still: a moment drawn at print resolution as PNG, PDF (TrimBox, BleedBox, crop marks) and CMYK TIFF (WP-23).

capabilities.capability: Gamma and quality settings per render.
capabilities.pro_use: Matching delivery colour and trading quality for speed in tests.

match.note: Draft versus final is a renderer and animatic choice; colour management is WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Introspection from the command line: list layers, targets, importers, value nodes, modules; print layer and canvas info.
capabilities.pro_use: Pipeline scripts checking what an installation can do.

match.note: Renderers and tools available, every command with its schema, and what is missing.

chapters.chapter: Export: Lottie, still images and interchange

capabilities.capability: Lottie export (1.4; under File > Export from 1.5.0) producing JSON, an HTML preview and a log of unsupported features; bones are not exported and spline shapes are baked per frame.
capabilities.pro_use: Animations for web pages and mobile apps.

match.note: Baked puppet animation as parented Lottie layers with views, swaps, lip-sync and springs; the web player export plays the whole film.

capabilities.capability: Lottie text layers (1.5.4) and a smaller-file mode that drops variable-width outlines (1.5.0).
capabilities.pro_use: Animated titles in apps; light files for the web.

match.note: export.lottie writes characters and the set image only; text, props and other elements in Lottie are renderer parity (WP-14); Lottie QA (lottie.qa) and dotLottie (lottie.dotlottie) exist (WP-23).

capabilities.capability: Exporting a still image of a chosen frame.
capabilities.pro_use: Thumbnails, posters and review stills.

match.note: Storyboard stills and scored cover frames per cut and platform; film.still makes print-ready stills at any resolution, and transparent ones of the characters alone (WP-23).

capabilities.capability: The native .sif/.sifz/.sfg file as an editable exchange format for other people and tools.
capabilities.pro_use: Handing a shot to an animator for hand finishing.

match.note: One shot as a .sif with one group per part and animated transforms, editable in Synfig Studio (bends, raster parts and dynamic z are not exported yet, WP-14).

capabilities.capability: Python 3 plugins run from the menu: Synfig hands the script a copy of the document file, then reloads the edited result.
capabilities.pro_use: Batch edits and pipeline automation inside the editor.

match.note: Every capability is an @command exposed to CLI, HTTP, MCP and Studio; agents edit film data directly.

capabilities.capability: Plugin metadata file declaring names (translatable) and exec, importer and exporter entries.
capabilities.pro_use: Distributing in-house tools to every seat.

match.note: Commands carry their own input schemas, listed by engine.commands; adding one is a decorated function.

capabilities.capability: Importer and exporter plugins that add file formats to File > Import and File > Export (1.5.0).
capabilities.pro_use: Supporting studio-specific or new formats.

match.note: Formats are commands; editor formats (FCPXML, EDL) are WP-22 and sticker and alpha formats WP-23 (sticker.pack, shot.alpha, film.formats, lottie.dotlottie).

capabilities.capability: Plugins with simple dialogs that receive the current time and the selected layer (1.5.3).
capabilities.pro_use: Context-aware tools such as 'add a blink here'.

match.note: Commands take times and frames as arguments; prose directions and frame notes become data edits.

capabilities.capability: Third-party plugins such as importing labels and timings from an audio editor, controller rigs and free-form deformation.
capabilities.pro_use: Bringing audio breakdowns in as timing marks; extra rigging aids.

match.note: Cue and music labels go out to Audacity (sound.audacity); importing labels back is WP-40.

capabilities.capability: Autosave and backups (on by default from 1.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Not losing work after a crash.

match.note: Every edit is a schema-checked file write in a git working tree; there is no unsaved editor state.

capabilities.capability: Unit system, default sizes and new-document settings (default background colour or image, 1.4).
capabilities.pro_use: House defaults for every new project.

match.note: New films start from defaults or a format template; brand kits are inherited per channel.

capabilities.capability: Experimental feature switches (the brush tool) and render thread count.
capabilities.pro_use: Opting into new features per seat.

match.note: Features are commands, enabled for all; worker count follows the CPU count.

capabilities.capability: Keyboard and mouse shortcuts, including new hotkeys for keyframe locks, duplicating layers and switching tabs (1.5.3, 1.5.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Speed for full-time artists.

match.note: Agent-driven; the Studio timeline has a few shortcuts (undo).

capabilities.capability: Icon themes chosen through an environment variable (1.5.0) and interface theming.
capabilities.pro_use: Comfort and accessibility of the interface.

match.note: Desktop UI theming.

capabilities.capability: Environment settings for external tools (for example the Python interpreter used by plugins).
capabilities.pro_use: Pointing the application at pipeline tool versions.

match.note: DBE_* environment variables name tool paths (Blender, Rhubarb, Python); the doctor reports and fixes them.

capabilities.capability: Bone morphing: a shape that changes between two drawn states as bones move.
capabilities.pro_use: Turning heads and changing silhouettes smoothly.

match.note: The turn control slides and parallaxes face parts for a 2.5D head turn and views switch; vector morphs between views are WP-43.

capabilities.capability: Reusing animations across files through exported values and imported canvases.
capabilities.pro_use: Building a motion library for a series.

match.note: Template clips and character clips play on every character of a template and in every renderer.

capabilities.capability: Symmetric patterns from one drawing with the duplicate layer (the snowflake).
capabilities.pro_use: Motion-design ornaments and kaleidoscopic effects.

match.note: Instancing and procedural repetition.

capabilities.capability: Subtracting shapes from each other with blend methods to cut holes.
capabilities.pro_use: Moons, donuts, cut-out lettering and shape booleans.

match.note: No shape booleans or alpha-subtract blends in puppet or shot data.
